option.label: Preparing text into token files
option.what: You would understand how raw text such as Shakespeare or OpenWebText is tokenized into binary train and validation files and read as batches.

ops.description: Why a model needs ids, and the simplest way to make them.
The small Shakespeare text is downloaded once and read into one long string. [files: data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py]
Unique characters are sorted and counted to give the vocabulary size. [files: data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py]
Two dictionaries map character to id and id to character, wrapped as an encoder and a decoder. [files: data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py]
How one long text becomes a training part and a validation part.
The first nine-tenths of the characters train and the last tenth validates. [files: data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py, data/shakespeare/prepare.py]

ops.text: Why validation text must stay unseen
ops.description: The validation part is a fair test only because the model never trains on it. [files: data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py]

ops.text: 3. Words in Pieces Instead of Letters
ops.description: The same text, tokenized with a fixed vocabulary of word pieces.
Compare the character vocabulary built from the text with a ready-made GPT-2 vocabulary. [files: data/shakespeare/prepare.py, data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py]
Train and validation text are each turned into lists of ids by the GPT-2 encoder. [files: data/shakespeare/prepare.py]
The printed counts, 301,966 for train and 36,059 for validation, show how many ids each file holds. [files: data/shakespeare/prepare.py]
Ids become plain binary files on disk.
Why the ids are stored as 16-bit unsigned numbers, and how that fits the GPT-2 vocabulary. [files: data/shakespeare/prepare.py]
Each array is written out raw as the train file and the validation file. [files: data/shakespeare/prepare.py]
The character version also saves its encoder, decoder and vocabulary size so text can be decoded again. [files: data/shakespeare_char/prepare.py]

ops.text: 5. Scaling Up to a Web-Sized Collection
ops.description: The same steps when the text is millions of documents.
The collection is loaded with several workers and holds only a training part at first. [files: data/openwebtext/prepare.py]
A tiny fraction of documents is shuffled out with a fixed seed and renamed as validation. [files: data/openwebtext/prepare.py]

ops.text: Tokenizing in parallel and writing to disk
ops.description: Documents are tokenized by several workers and the ids are written into a large binary file. [files: data/openwebtext/prepare.py]
How the binary files become the examples the model sees.

ops.text: Opening a file without loading it all
ops.description: The token file is mapped from disk so a huge file does not have to fit in memory. [files: train.py]
Random start positions each give a block of consecutive ids, stacked into a batch. [files: train.py]

ops.text: Targets are the inputs shifted by one
ops.description: Each target is the next token after its input, so every position is a prediction task. [files: train.py]
